conclusions: Reject C3 and restore the exact accepted C2 buried-volume source. The required incremental batch wall reduction fails at both thread settings and in both launch orders. No supplementary timing is needed to establish this negative decision.

Target wall medians are slower by about 15.6 percent, with all serial pairs slower and six of eight six-thread pairs slower. All 16 target CPU pairs are slower. The broad six-thread wall range does not erase the serial regression or CPU evidence.
Conformer, ensemble and database-build incremental medians also regress at both thread settings. Parsing has smaller negative wall and CPU medians. Every value and range is retained.

Screening is approximately CPU-neutral incrementally with mixed wall results. Search has highly dispersed wall results, negative medians and smaller CPU costs. Do not claim a search improvement or infer a specific cause from these observations.
The remaining cumulative parallel batch and screening gains include accepted C1/C2 changes. They cannot count as C3 benefit.

The actual operation probe confirms 45.4505 percent fewer Z predicates including endpoint predicates and 33.6009 percent fewer combined XY/Z operations under that explicit model. It excludes other added traversal, finite-check, branch and machine costs; the native measurements refute the speed hypothesis.

All scientific gates passed. This is a performance rejection, not an observed scientific-output failure. Keep the patch, six new focused test groups, frozen build and all successful/failed harness evidence; preserve existing scientific-method limits.
Both analyses verified live C3 source and complete postflight before permission to restore C2 was sent. This interpretation reads their sealed receipts and does not require C3 to remain live.

predeclared_target.metric: descriptors_10000 native wall time versus contemporaneously measured accepted C2 at both one and six threads

statistical_policy: Every predeclared measured pair is retained. Warmups are verified and retained separately. Medians, MAD, full ranges and AB/BA effects are descriptive; no confidence-interval, universal improvement or changed acceptance-threshold claim is introduced.
